summary: PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 is a detailed and largely faithful extraction. The review corrected it carefully against the Annals text, and its main theorems stand: 4.4, 5.8, 6.5 and 8.10. I re-read the published version in full and the preprint where items or issues depend on it; both hashes match the recorded ones. I checked every cited layer, every library declaration at the pinned commits, all 53 source issues and the neighbouring extractions. There are 13 findings: 8 medium and 5 low. Medium: (1) Feng 24's later review gave the general form of §3.4 (Tate diagonal, unique extension of characters) and the Frobenius twist of algebras to SheafTheoreticSmithTheory, and said this Part II imports them; route 1 still plans items 2 and 26 and says so in its brief. (2) Item 3 (nonabelian H^1) is a special case of the Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 5 plan. (3) Lang–Steinberg, Steinberg's σ-stable Borel pairs and the closedness of the class of σ are used in Propositions 5.6 and 8.3 but have no item; the first is now planned at RG2.3. (4) Item 16 is 'library' but its module structures are not in the libraries, apart from Tau Ceti's LeftCosetModule for X = G, and the review's own split was never made. (5) The 'planned' statuses of items 37 and 43 (and the citations of 38 and 18) are wrong, as the review's notes said, but were not changed. (6) Route 1's brief narrows Theorem 5.8 to semisimple G, although the paper proves it for reductive G and the §9.4–9.5 examples need that. (7) New source issue: the canonical pseudoroot (b) of §9.3 (the Hecke character 𝔭 ↦ N𝔭) squares to δ^{-1}, so for p ≥ 7 it is not a pseudoroot (SL_2, p = 7, q_v = 3); item 59 copies it and E32's correction does not reach it. (8) Review-added example items restate each other in pairs, and one says n ≥ 1 where σ is trivial for n = 1. Low: Proposition 5.4 needs K′ normal in K; the Steinberg citation [34, p. 173] points outside pp. 49–80; the canonical torus, C-group and torus Langlands correspondence have no single owner across TV, FKP-22 and PQ-26; stale 'published text could not be read' records, and no sourceVersions although three issues affect stated results; three missing prerequisites (Henniart–Vignéras, Rohlfs–Speh, Steinberg 1968). E1–E53 were checked; the key ones were recomputed (E7, E9–E11, E13, E19, E32, E38, E42, E50, E51), and none is wrong. No route goes into a finished blueprint, and there is no cycle. This session wrote FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1, whose proposed edits to AA.4, SR.4 and ALS.0 touch layers cited in finding 5; none of those edits plans the statements at issue. No finding touches BHKT-19.

The string cc-f805bf occurs in none of the .md, .result.json, .review.json, the review report or the register entries, so this session did none of that work.

Disclosure. This session wrote FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1 (fixes report of 29 September). It proposes edits to AA.4, SR.4, ALS.0 and AF.2, among others. Finding 5 cites the current texts of AA.0, AA.1, AA.3, AA.4, ALS.3 and SR.4. None of that report's proposed edits plans the restricted tensor product of Hecke algebras, the properness of H(F)\H(A) → G(F)\G(A), or the singular-chain/correspondence comparison, so it does not affect the findings. This session also red-teamed BHKT-19 (PR #4725). No finding here touches BHKT-19. RT-AREA-automorphic-1 (by cc-39fac3) did not attack this paper: it withheld it as the coordinator's review.

Source, version of record. Ann. of Math. 183 (2016), 177–228, doi:10.4007/annals.2016.183.1.4, from https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v183-n1-p04-p.pdf, fetched 30 September 2026. 52 pages, SHA-256 15513caba4eed4f9b71c7d1ec791c0c406bb32e7a539ddf63d1a24d227863355, equal to the review's recorded 15513cab…. Read in full through pdftotext (the PDF is not an obstacle to text extraction), §§1–9 and the references.

Source, preprint. arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2346v1 (55 pp., SHA-256 34e2416f08ba0dc4a4fb8369875ef3d9f5a5b2ef8290733545442801baec9ee8) and source archive https://arxiv.org/e-print/1407.2346v1 (SHA-256 28e20b81414249488dc37189de7ffeb316314c5c3ea374fe675a5e28195b2c11, equal to the extraction's), fetched 30 September 2026. The arXiv API (30 September 2026) lists only v1. Collated with print where items or findings depend on it: §§2.12–2.13, §7.5 and §7.8 (preprint numbering), §§9–12 (Theorem 9.1, the tables, Propositions 10.3, 10.6, 11.2, 12.3), the bibliography, and the Steinberg citations. No erratum or corrigendum is linked from the Annals article page.

Mathematics recomputed. The published (7.2.1) twist, with PGL_2 and T = 1_{K diag(ϖ,1) K}: S*(T) = qa + a^{-1} is invariant under a ↦ 1/(qa), not q/a, which confirms E32. That (7.4)(b)(i) δ = |Σ_G|_v has parameter Σ*_G(q_v)^{-1} under (2.9.2). E19's GL_1×GL_1 counterexample and the correctness of the norm-product formula for br (additivity modulo N·A). E7's SO(3,1) counterexample. E9 (PGL_2, P = G). E10 and E11 (left/right action, dependence on representatives). E13's three-chain example. E38 (order-2 elements of SL_2 in characteristic 3). E42 (squared length 7264 of the printed Σ_H against 78 for both corrected vectors, with even pairings, in the E_7 Cartan form). E50 (SL_3 ⊃ GL_2). E51 (the norm on the Sp_2n torus). §9.7's root geometry (β_2 = β_1 + 3α, (β_1+3α)^∨ = β_1^∨ + α^∨, Σ_H/2 = 2β_1 + 3α, Σ_G/2 = 5α + 3β_1, and ⟨β_1, α^∨⟩ = −3 making β_{1,*}(−1) non-central in L̂_o). §9.5 and §9.6's admissible tuples. Lemma 8.8's perturbation argument. The rev-linkage item (N = (1−σ)^{p−1}). And the σ-triviality for SL_2 (finding 8).

Every item (121) against the published text, with statuses and routes. Every missing item is routed exactly once, with no multiple routing; the two planned items in route 3 (45, 56) are legitimate source uses. Library claims read at the pinned commits (declarations.tsv and the files): Mathlib 082e2d3 WittVector (RingTheory/WittVector/Defs.lean:52), WittVector.frobenius (Frobenius.lean:221), WittVector.teichmuller (Teichmuller.lean:93), WittVector.isDiscreteValuationRing (DiscreteValuationRing.lean:149), tateCohomology (RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/Basic.lean:145), Rep.tateNorm (:63), TateCohomology.δ (:199), exact₁ (:217), exact₃ (:213), IsHeckeTriple (NumberTheory/HeckeRing/Defs.lean:75), HeckeRing (:189), HeckeCosetModule (:183), modularCyclotomicCharacter (NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:212). Tau Ceti f790474 TauCeti.TateCohomology.H0IsoNormQuotient (RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/LowDegree.lean:88), HNegOneIsoNormKernelQuotient (:181), Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.periodicIso (Periodic.lean:341), HeckeCosetModule.instRingHeckeRing (NumberTheory/HeckeRing/Associativity.lean:485), HeckeAntiInvolution.bar (Commutativity.lean:98), HeckeCosetModule.commSemiringOfAntiInvolution (Commutativity.lean:478), and the uncited LeftCosetModule (LeftCosetModule/Basic.lean:296, :314; Action.lean:383). All exist as cited; the one over-claim is finding 4.

Searches for items marked missing that the libraries might have. Nonabelian group H^1: none (only Mathlib's Čech H1 for presheaves of groups, and Tau Ceti's abelian continuous cohomology). Lang's theorem, Frobenius twist of modules, Tate diagonal, fundamental domains for free Z/p actions on ℓ-spaces, unramified characters of tori, Brauer homomorphism, Smith theory, Satake with k-coefficients: none. The missing statuses of items 2–5, 14, 15, 17, 23–35 and 39–107 stand, except item 3 (finding 2).

Every cited layer read in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.0–AA.5, ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0–ALS.6, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0–SR.6, and ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.1, RG2.3, RG2.4, RG2.5. Also content/tau-ceti/ReductiveGroups/README.md Layers 7 and 9 (root datum with Galois action, parabolics and Levis, pinned Chevalley–Demazure groups, Frobenius, special isogenies in characteristics 2 and 3). The planned statuses of items 6, 8–13, 36, 45, 53 and 56 are acceptable. Items 37, 38, 43 and 18 are finding 5. There are no packets or decompositions for AA, ALS, SR or RG2, so no route goes into a finished blueprint. No DESIGN job exists yet for either Part II (queue.json), so there is nothing downstream to break.

Duplication against other extractions: PAPER-FENG-24 (all four routes, the review and the item notes on TV), PAPER-VENKATESH-19 (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpacesPartII: derived Hecke algebra, disjoint from route 1 as its reason says), PAPER-SCHOLZE-15 and PAPER-CARAIANI-SCHOLZE-17 (torsion Galois representations; TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure TC.0–TC.4, no overlap with Smith theory), PAPER-GAN-HARRIS-SAWIN-ETAL-24, PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18 (Lang's theorem), PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22 (canonical torus), PAPER-PASKUNAS-QUAST-26 (C-group, Langlands for tori), and every Part II or new route whose parent or title touches ReductiveGroups, SmoothRepresentations or ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces. Also searches of all item names across research/blueprint/papers for Brauer homomorphism, linkage, plain subgroups, Smith theory, pseudoroots, C-group, canonical torus, Borel–de Siebenthal, prime-order automorphisms, Tate cohomology and Frobenius twist. Findings 1, 2, 3 and 11 come from this. Feng's route 3 (ModPBernsteinCentersAndLocalBaseChange) correctly imports plain subgroups, Br, linkage and the conjecture from route 1.

Routes: the three routes, their owners and their briefs against PROTOCOL §§15–16. Route 1 as a Part II of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces and route 2 as a Part II of Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups are both justified; route 3 as a source for SR.0, SR.1, SR.2 and SR.4 is justified. There is no stage-level cycle. Item 65 (the c-group Satake isomorphism, route 3 → SR.4) needs the c-group of item 63 (route 2), which in turn imports SR.4. That is only a roadmap-level mutual dependency, harmless if the c-group is an early layer of route 2 (finding 11 names an owner). The briefs' final theorems were checked against print (Theorems 4.4, 5.8, 6.5, the Theorem of §8.1 = 8.10, and 9.1 with its E6 exceptions), which gives finding 6.

Source issues E1–E53: each read at its locator in the version it names. Of E1–E4 (preprint-only) and E17, E18 and E39–E49, I checked the printed text of E1, E2, E3, E42, E45 (the printed '1720'), E47 and E49 in the preprint PDF. E5–E16 and E19–E38, E50–E53 were checked against the published text. The substantive ones were re-derived as listed above. All confirmations stand. A search for missed mistakes gave findings 7, 9 and 10. The review's changes were checked for errors they introduced: E32's correction is right but does not propagate to §9.3(b) (finding 7), and the review-added example items contain the n ≥ 1 slip (finding 8). The corrections to items 12, 16, 17, 18, 30, 32, 33, 35, 41, 55, 56, 58, 59, 60 and 64 were verified. Missing sourceVersions and stale records: finding 12.

findings.where: PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16/3 (nonabelian cohomology of a cyclic group of order p), status missing, route 1
findings.claim: Item 3 is marked missing and route 1 plans it. But the Tau Ceti EllipticCurves roadmap, which is existing work, plans continuous nonabelian H^1 of a profinite group acting on a discrete group: cocycles, coboundaries, the pointed set, functoriality and restriction. Item 3's H^1(σ; M) is the case G = ⟨σ⟩ (finite, hence profinite) with M discrete, where continuity is automatic. Only the cyclic-group reformulations are specific to this paper: evaluation at σ, and the description as M-conjugacy classes of elements mσ of order p. The five-term exact sequence (item 4) and the prime-to-p invariance (item 5) are not in that layer's list, so they stay missing.
findings.evidence: content/tau-ceti/EllipticCurves/README.md, Layer 5 (stage tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-5-twists-aec-x2-x5): 'the full nonabelian-H¹ classification is a stretch milestone, and the continuous nonabelian H¹ prerequisite (spelled out in §Layer 7's dependency note) is this layer's'. Layer 7's note: 'That material is a prerequisite lane of its own, needed by Layer 5 …: continuous nonabelian 1-cocycles, the coboundary equivalence, the pointed set H¹_cts(G, A), functoriality and restriction, and the reduction to finite quotients for profinite G and discrete A.' Paper, published §2.2, p. 184: 'we let H^1(σ; M) denote the nonabelian cohomology of ⟨σ⟩ with coefficients in M, i.e., cocycles j : ⟨σ⟩ → M modulo coboundaries.' Neither library has it at the pinned commits: Mathlib 082e2d3's Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/NonabelianCohomology/H1.lean is Čech-type H^1 of a presheaf of groups, and declarations.tsv has no nonabelian group H^1 in Mathlib or Tau Ceti f790474.
findings.fix: Item 3: status planned, planned ['tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-5-twists-aec-x2-x5']. Note: 'the definition is the case G = ⟨σ⟩, A = M discrete of Layer 5's H¹_cts(G, A); the evaluation-at-σ and M⋊⟨σ⟩ descriptions are this paper's and are planned with item 4 in route 1'. Remove item 3 from route 1's items. Route 1's brief should import nonabelian H^1 from that layer, and keep the exact sequence (item 4), the prime-to-p statement (item 5, in its profinite form) and the cyclic-group descriptions. Because the Tau Ceti roadmap labels the milestone 'stretch', the brief should say that route 1 needs only the finite-group case and may build it there if Layer 5 has not, citing Layer 5 as the owner.

findings.where: PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 items (none); proofs of Proposition 5.6 (item 41) and Proposition 8.3 (item 68); route 1 and route 2 briefs
findings.claim: Three theorems that the proofs use have no item and no owner in either brief. (a) Lang–Steinberg: H^1(F_v, H) = 0 for a connected smooth group over a finite field. It is the key step of Proposition 5.6, and E27 turns on its hypothesis that the special fibre is connected. PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18 has since routed it to ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3, so it should be recorded as planned there and imported. (b) Steinberg's theorem that a finite-order (semisimple) automorphism σ of a connected reductive group stabilises a Borel pair, and in fact one containing a given σ-fixed regular semisimple element. It is the first step of Proposition 8.3, on which all of §8 rests. (c) Closedness in characteristic 0 of the conjugacy class of the finite-order automorphism σ in the non-connected group G⋊⟨σ⟩ (Joyner). The proof of Proposition 5.6 uses it to make the image of g ↦ g^{-1}σ(g) closed. No layer of the atlas and neither library plans (b) or (c).
findings.evidence: Published §5.6, proof, p. 198: 'in characteristic zero, the conjugacy class of σ is closed. ([22, Cor. 5.8]: σ is automatically semisimple, being of finite order.)' and 'Steinberg's theorem [34, Th. 1.9] says that the Galois cohomology of the connected algebraic group H is trivial over the finite field F_v.' Published §8.3, proof, p. 212: 'Let x ∈ T_H be a regular semisimple element of H. By [35, §8.9], we may find a σ-stable maximal torus and Borel of G containing x.' (the preprint also cites Reeder, Lemma 3.2). Owner of (a): PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18/lang-theorem ('Let G be a smooth connected algebraic group over a finite field k. Then H^1(k, G) = 0 …', status missing, route 12 = source to ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3; its review was merged 24 September 2026). For (b) and (c), searches of every stage description in data/atlas.json (quasi-semisimple, stable Borel, semisimple automorphism, closed conjugacy class) and of every paper extraction's item names found nothing. Neither does the Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups README, Layers 0–9. The items of this extraction mention (a)–(c) only inside the notes of items 41 and 68.
findings.fix: Add three items. (a) 'Lang–Steinberg: for H a smooth connected group over a finite field κ, H^1(κ, H) = 0; hence a torsor under such a group has a κ-point' (locator: published §5.6 proof, p. 198, citing Steinberg, Regular elements, Th. 1.9), status planned ['ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3'] via PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18's source route; add RG2.3 to route 1's imports. (b) 'Steinberg: an automorphism σ of finite order of a connected reductive group G over an algebraically closed field stabilises a Borel subgroup and a maximal torus in it; if x ∈ G^σ is regular semisimple, the pair can be chosen to contain x' (published §8.3 proof, p. 212, citing Steinberg, Endomorphisms of linear algebraic groups, §8.9, and in the preprint also Reeder, Lemma 3.2), status missing, route 2. (c) 'In characteristic 0, the G-conjugacy class of a finite-order element of G⋊⟨σ⟩ is closed' (published §5.6 proof, p. 198, citing Joyner, Cor. 5.8), status missing, route 1. Add Steinberg's memoir, Regular elements and Joyner to prerequisites if they are not covered (see finding 13).

findings.claim: Item 16 is marked library, but its statement includes two module structures: the right H(G,K)-module V^K (corrected (2.10.2)) and the right H(G,K)-module k[X/K] for a right G-set X ((2.10.3)). Neither library has these in general. The cited declarations give the double-coset ring and its anti-involution. Tau Ceti also has the case X = G, k[G/K] as a module over the opposite Hecke ring, which the item does not cite. The review itself ruled that the status is library 'only for the algebra' and told the fixer to split off the module structures as a missing construction for route 1. That was not done, so the module structures that §2.11, (4.2.2) and (6.2.1) use are neither in the libraries nor routed. The review's remark that 'Neither library has the right module structures' is also too strong, because of the X = G case.

Neither library has the right module structures on V^K and k[X/K]. … So the status is library only for the algebra: split off the two module structures as a missing construction (route 1, which consumes them in §§2.11 and 4).' The item is still 'library' and still states both module structures, and no rev- item was added for them. findings.where: PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16/37 (planned AA.0, AA.4), PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16/43 (planned AA.3), PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16/38 (planned RG2.3, SR.4), PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16/18 (planned ALS.1, ALS.3)
findings.claim: The review found that several 'planned' statuses do not hold, said how to fix each one in the item notes, and left the statuses unchanged. Re-reading the layer texts confirms two of them. Item 37: the restricted tensor product H(G(A_f),K) = ⊗'_v H(G_v,K_v) of k-valued Hecke algebras is planned by neither AA.0 nor AA.4. Item 43: properness of H(F)\H(A) → G(F)\G(A) for a reductive subgroup H is not planned by AA.3. For item 38, the review said nothing plans 'all but finitely many places are good'. In fact AA.1's spreading-out model gives the hyperspecial part, and Lang's theorem (finding 3) gives quasi-splitness, so the item should cite AA.1 rather than be split. For item 18, the review noted that ALS.3 builds Hecke operators as correspondences through K∩gKg^{-1}, not by (2.10.3) on singular simplices, and that the comparison is needed. No layer plans that comparison.
findings.evidence: Stage texts (research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/AdelicAlgebraicGroups.json): AA.0 'Starting with the existing restricted-product topology, prove continuity of multiplication and inversion, local compactness, compact-open cylinders … restricted products of Haar measures'; AA.3 'Construct minimal rational parabolics, relative positive chambers, Siegel sets … finite volume … compactness of the appropriate quotient for F-anisotropic groups …'; AA.4 'weak approximation … strong approximation … finite covering maps for nested compact opens … Cartesian diagrams for Hecke correspondences'; AA.1 'Prove independence of spreading-out model and finite exceptional set.' ALS.3: 'For g and K construct the two finite-level maps through K∩gKg⁻¹, pullback and trace, and their induced chain maps.' Review notes left unapplied. Item 37: 'Neither states the restricted-tensor-product decomposition … Either cite AF.0 and SR.1, or mark the item missing and route it to route 1.' findings.where: PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16/59 (global and canonical pseudoroots) and sourceIssues (new E54); published §9.3(b) and (9.3.1), p. 221; preprint §7.5(b) and (7.5.1), pp. 27–28
findings.claim: Canonical pseudoroot (b) is defined as the pullback along Σ_G/2 of the 'cyclotomic' idele class character, and the paper says that character 'corresponds to the Hecke character that sends a prime-to-p ideal to its norm'. With the standard dictionary χ(𝔭_v) = χ_v(ϖ_v), its component at v is x ↦ q_v^{v(x)} = |x|_v^{-1}. So the pulled-back character χ0 = cyc∘(Σ_G/2) satisfies χ0^2 = |Σ_G|_v^{-1} = δ^{-1}, not δ. The paper's own definition of a pseudoroot (§7.4(b)(i), '(δ^{1/2})^2 = δ' with δ = |Σ_G|_v) therefore fails whenever q_v^{2⟨Σ_G,λ⟩} ≠ 1 in k. Since ⟨Σ_G, α^∨⟩ = 2 for a simple coroot, that means whenever q_v^4 ≢ 1 mod p, which happens at a set of places of positive density as soon as p ≥ 7. Concretely, for G = SL_2, F = Q, p = 7, v = 3 and t = diag(3,1/3): δ(t) = |9|_3 = 1/9 ≡ 4 mod 7, while χ0(t)^2 = 3^2 ≡ 2 mod 7. The formula (9.3.1) ρ^-_G(Frob_v) = Σ*_G/2(cyclo(Frob_v))⋊Frob_v agrees with the definition of ρ^- (the parameter of χ0^{-1}, (7.5.4)) only for the inverse character. That holds with Frob_v arithmetic, as E32's correction requires (α0 = Σ*_G(√q_v)^{-1}). So the parenthetical, not (9.3.1), is what needs changing, and E32's correction does not reach it. This is not recorded among E1–E53. The review's note on item 59 treats it as a matter of convention, but the parenthetical fixes the convention. The paper's examples are unaffected, because they have p = 2 (case (a)) or p = 3 (q_v^4 ≡ 1). Item 59 as written defines, for p ≥ 7, a character that is not a pseudoroot.
findings.evidence: Published p. 221: '(b) When the half-sum of positive roots Σ_G/2 : T^can_G → G_m exists in the character lattice for T^can_G: In this case, we obtain the canonical pseudoroot by pulling back the “cyclotomic” idele class character of G_m(A) → k^* via Σ_G/2. (The “cyclotomic” idele class character corresponds to the Hecke character that sends a prime-to-p ideal to its norm in k^*.)' and '(9.3.1) ρ^-_G(γ) = γ, case (a); Σ*_G/2(cyclo(γ)) ⋊ γ, case (b)'. Published §7.4(b), p. 209: 'we get the “k-valued modular character” (7.4.2) δ : B_v → F_v^* →(|·|_v) q_v^Z → k^* or δ = |Σ_G|_v for short. Then we should have (i) (δ^{1/2})^2 = δ'. §9 preamble, p. 220: a global pseudoroot is 'a k^*-valued idele class character of T^can_G … which restricts to a local pseudoroot at almost every good place v'. Preprint p. 27 has the same parenthetical, with '(7.5.1) ρ_G : γ ↦ Σ*_G/2(cyclo(γ)) ⋊ γ'. Item 59 repeats '(b) … the pullback along Σ_G/2 of the cyclotomic idele class character, which corresponds to the Hecke character sending a prime-to-p ideal to its norm in k^*'. The SL_2 computation is above. Its only convention is the standard ideal–idele dictionary, which the paper does not override.
findings.fix: Item 59, (b): replace 'the pullback along Σ_G/2 of the cyclotomic idele class character, which corresponds to the Hecke character sending a prime-to-p ideal to its norm in k^*' with 'the pullback along Σ_G/2 of the idele class character |·|_A mod p, which corresponds to the Hecke character sending a prime-to-p ideal 𝔭 to N𝔭^{-1} in k^* (its component at v is x ↦ q_v^{-v(x)}, so the pullback squares to δ = |Σ_G|_v); with Frob_v the arithmetic Frobenius, ρ^-_G(Frob_v) = (Σ*_G/2)(q_v)⋊Frob_v = (Σ*_G/2)(cyclo(Frob_v))⋊Frob_v, as (9.3.1) states'. findings.claim: rev-exotic-mod-2-transfer-from starts 'Let F be a number field, n ≥ 1, G = SL_2n …, σ(g) = J(g^T)^{-1}J^{-1}, an automorphism of order 2'. For n = 1 this σ is the identity, because J g J^{-1} = (g^T)^{-1} for every g ∈ SL_2. So the item's hypothesis 'of order 2' fails there, and the construction of §4 does not apply. Its companion rev-exotic-transfer-from-sp-2n correctly says 'n ≥ 2 … (for n = 1, σ is trivial)'. Both items were added by the review, and each of the three pairs states the same σ-dual homomorphism and its consequence twice, in different words. The review's own note asked that the global item 'should cite it rather than restate it'. As things stand, route 2 lists each result twice, once with an error.
findings.evidence: rev-exotic-mod-2-transfer-from (statement): 'Let F be a number field, n ≥ 1, G = SL_2n split over F, J ∈ SL_2n(Z) the standard skew-symmetric matrix, and σ(g) = J(g^T)^{-1}J^{-1}, an automorphism of order 2 with G^σ = H ≅ Sp_2n.' rev-exotic-transfer-from-sp-2n: 'Let n ≥ 2 … (for n = 1, σ is trivial)'. findings.claim: Proposition 5.4 allows any K′ = ∏K′_v ⊂ K with K′_v = K_v on V. For K′ not normal in K, the quotient K/K′ is not a group and no argument is given. Item 39 copies the statement without the hypothesis. The only use is §5.5(d), where a normal K′ can always be chosen, so no later result is affected. Neither the extraction nor the review recorded this.
